title: Certifiable Artificial Intelligence Through Data Fusion
venue: AAAI FSS-21: Artificial Intelligence in Government and Public Sector
extended_summary:
This paper is a conceptual and position-oriented review of how artificial intelligence systems can be certified for adoption, fielding, and maintenance. The authors argue that rapid progress in AI has outpaced the development of standardized processes for determining performance bounds, explaining system behavior, and managing expectations of intended use. To address this gap, the paper proposes using test-and-evaluation methods drawn from systems engineering, along with a Multisource AI Scorecard Table (MAST), to assess AI systems across inputs, uncertainty, interpretability, transparency, and outputs.

The main approach is not an educational intervention but a certification framework for AI/ML systems. The paper discusses how model cards, uncertainty analysis, verification and validation, and robustness testing can be combined to support certifiable AI. It also distinguishes between quantitative performance measures and qualitative considerations such as explainability and trust, and emphasizes that certification must be tied to the system’s intended use and operating conditions.

The paper includes a notional image-fusion use case involving automatic target recognition with infrared and visible imagery. Using this example, the authors illustrate how different image-fusion methods can be compared on performance metrics and how performance bounds may define a certifiable region for deployment. The conclusion is that AI certification should account for data, model behavior, user interaction, and operational context, and that current standards need further refinement to support dynamic AI systems.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/review paper proposing certification frameworks, not an empirical study of K-12 learners or educational interventions. It contains no experimental design, comparison group, or outcome evaluation relevant to the target domain.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact is measured or demonstrated. The paper discusses AI certification and safety considerations in general technical terms, with no evidence of effect on K-12 science inquiry supports or learner outcomes.

interventions.use_case: certifiability and verification of AI/ML systems for image data fusion, with a notional automatic target recognition (ATR) use case using CNN-based multimodal infrared and visible image fusion
